title: LEAP: LLM Inference on Scalable PIM-NoC Architecture with Balanced Dataflow and Fine-Grained Parallelism
problem: LLM inference requires massive memory bandwidth and communication overhead that exceeds GPU capabilities in latency and energy.
motivation: Processing-In-Memory architectures combined with optimized NoC can overcome memory bottlenecks in LLM inference.
method: LEAP designs a chip that puts processing elements directly at memory (called processing-in-memory) and connects them with an on-chip network, built from scratch for language models. This avoids the common problem where data travels far from memory to a distant processor, wasting time and energy. The system spreads work evenly across many processors so nothing waits for data, and adjusts automatically whether you run a small or large model.
key_novelty: The core innovation is putting processing right at memory with an on-chip network, both designed together specifically for language models, so work distributes evenly and prevents bottlenecks.
limitations: Comparison primarily against A100; evaluation against other PIM architectures limited.
primary_theme: PIM-NoC architecture for LLM inference acceleration
